literature_window.rule: First-release dates, recent venue/journal editions of older preprints, code releases and unverified publication dates are distinct. A code commit is not a publication date.

scope: Comprehensive inventory for ten reviewed TDN experiment groups and the retrieved recent primary-source corpus. It does not assert completeness over all world literature or all unexecuted code paths. Small CPU mathematical checks support derivations; no new model training, fresh confirmation campaign or native GPU run.
main_conclusion: The project has strong structural correctness, honest negative endpoints and useful source/pair inductive biases; no trained full solver utility gate passes. Next focus headroom over best bareDF, spatial-target consistency, finite-step stiffness/order safety, independentfieldreplication andtotaldeploymentcost.

experiments.name: Initial/light screens
experiments.evidence_class: native CARC CPU output plus committed cloud validation
experiments.observed: Historical G2/G4 failed; native light output reported six accepted references, zero numerical-headroom cases and five temporal-oracle advantages. No joint candidate.
experiments.limitation: Six cases reuse two states; the committed light validation is cloud CPU, not the native job. Tiny temporal oracle fits cannot rank deployed solvers.

experiments.name: First frozen A100 neural benchmark
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual CARC A100 execution
experiments.observed: 35 GPU tests; 9 diagnostic parents and one training initialization. Reaction-clock has 0 speed wins against the best classical method; the original temporal MLP loses all 7 eligible speed comparisons against generic MLP. Clock stiff-boundary one-step RMS is 0.04872 against the 0.002 target.
experiments.limitation: 96 updates, unequal capacities, a 32-square grid with batch size 1, and three timing repeats. Reference-informed horizon choice can mask transients.

experiments.name: Three-seed neural replication
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual CARC CPU execution; separate A100 replication log in user conversation
experiments.observed: 386 CPU tests; 225/225 references accepted; 15 checkpoint selections, 14 trained. Clock jointly passes transient tests on 6/6/5 of 27 parents across the seeds; FNO-split passes 9/10/9. No learned family jointly passes boundary parents. Clock speed wins against the best classical method are 0/0/1.
experiments.limitation: The committed reviewed JSON records CPU execution. The user A100 log similarly reported 6/6/5 and 9/10/9, but a complete independently reviewed uploaded A100 replication archive is absent here. Three seeds share 27 parents; these are not 81 independent and identically distributed samples.

experiments.name: Training-free mechanism audit
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual CARC CPU execution
experiments.observed: 600/600 cases, 103 tests, and 40 accepted coupled references. Clock cannot generate the required cubic boundary correction; 24 remote cases have a zero receiver gate. The pair-aware oracle is best in 21/24 cases, with median normalized held-out kernel error 0.151 against scalar error 0.672.
experiments.limitation: Case-specific oracle coefficients and privileged pair/background labels make this a representation probe rather than a learned comparison. Capacity attenuates leading coefficients and does not guarantee accuracy.

experiments.name: Field-derived interaction screen
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual CARC CPU execution
experiments.observed: 502 records, 188 tests, and 32 references. GL3 improves on Strang in 32/32 cases, with median L2 error ratio 0.02742; it wins 23/32 accuracy comparisons against ETDRK4. ETDRK4 is more accurate and faster in all 3 historical 2D cases. GL3 per-step cost is 5.846 times Strang and 1.789 times ETDRK4.
experiments.limitation: Single sequential, uncached timing samples. Mean error accounts for 92.54% of split squared error, but mean-only loses most ETDRK4 comparisons. Every Strang L2 error is already below 0.002, so that target gives no efficiency headroom.

experiments.name: Prepared work–precision
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual CARC CPU execution
experiments.observed: 1008 candidates, 302 tests, and 240 parity checks. There are 23 accepted conditions; one frozen reference exceeds its budget by 12.17%, excluding 56 frontiers. Warmed fastest-method counts across 184 targets are Strang 102 / ETDRK4 73 / GL3 8 / GL5 1; setup-inclusive counts are 135/40/8/1. The spectral mean identity agrees to approximately 1e-15 but yields no global wins.
experiments.limitation: The mean-only correction leaves 99.9433% of its remaining error energy in the spatial component at one step. Full GL3 late apparent order is 1.88 versus ETDRK4 3.98. Five repeats and a single setup estimate do not establish timing uncertainty. Same-grid reference uncertainty is not a continuum certificate.

experiments.name: Compact-spatial accuracy/scaling
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual CARC CPU execution
experiments.observed: 2760 candidates, 281 tests, 166 references, and 392 parity checks. Fused GL3 is a median 1.587 times faster than original GL3, with parity error 3e-15. Input cutoffs are never the fastest complete solver; the high input modes 9/10 generate interaction mode 1, which truncation discards. K=8 high-pair error is 20.7 times GL3, and near-Nyquist error is approximately 156 times higher. Scaling Strang errors are already 7.7 times below the tightest target.
experiments.limitation: Fusion reverses its speed advantage at a 64-square grid and batch size 16. Small-grid cutoff methods cost approximately 1.89 times fused GL3. The quadratic branch remains approximately second order in time. Smooth scaling tests measure throughput without demonstrating accuracy headroom.

experiments.name: Fedora premix
experiments.evidence_class: uploaded actual Fedora RTX4090 run; independently rehashed now
experiments.observed: 61 scientific file hashes verified; 434 CPU / 27 GPU tests; 240 accepted neural references. There are 15 trials, 14 trained selections, 2592 candidates, and 48 diagnostic parents. At RMS 2e-4, premix coverage is 16/12/12 versus FNO 32/24/16; classical ETDRK4 and GL3 each cover 48/48. Output projection preserves low-frequency interaction coefficients, but direct selected convolution costs approximately 2 times the full FFT output method in 1D and 10 times in 2D.
experiments.limitation: Mixing before compression improves validation but does not establish held-out dominance. Full output projection still computes full GL3. FNO capacity is unequal: 23825 versus 67137 parameters. Different fields at different grids do not isolate resolution transfer. Mean drift and missing exact null limits motivate the consistency experiment.

experiments.name: Fedora physical consistency
experiments.evidence_class: uploaded actual Fedora RTX4090 run; independently rehashed now
experiments.observed: 69 scientific files verified; 304 CPU / 38 GPU tests; 456 references. There are 21 trials, 14 trained selections, 7 initializations, and 3456 candidates. Constrained moment backbones each cover 40/48 at RMS 2e-4; all neural arms cover 36/48 at maximum error 2e-4. Premix moment coverage at strict RMS 2e-6 is 22/28/12 versus FNO 24/28/12. GL3 covers 44/48 at RMS 2e-6.
experiments.limitation: The mean head adds approximately 22% same-step overhead to premix and 13.5% to FNO. Stiff premix cases require more steps. Constraints benefit both backbones. All diagnostic step queries were used during development, and grids are not paired discretizations. Seven initialization selections cannot establish learning.

experiments.name: Full Fedora research agenda
experiments.evidence_class: reviewed uploaded actual Fedora RTX4090 full run
experiments.observed: 8 complete, sealed stages and 341 scientific files; 222 structural cases with 34 required passes; 744 references; 69 trials with 64 trained selections and 5 initializations. All 152 GPU tests pass at each of 6 stages. None of 24 joint criteria passes. Diffusion-first orientation improves validation by a factor of 23.68. Source RMS 2e-4 coverage is 574/576 versus FNO 576/576; maximum-error 2e-5 coverage is 477/576 versus 533/576; rank-2 covers 176/192. Bare diffusion-first Strang is approximately 3.9 times faster than Source/rank-2. Discrete false accepts are 0/1179; continuum failures are 306/410 accepted predictions.
experiments.limitation: 8 controlled fields share 1 phase-seed cluster. Rank-2 has only one training seed; the cheap one-layer FNO is not confirmed. The continuum subset contains 8 parents under one physics choice. Policy costs are attributed components rather than independently timed standalone deployment. RF-optimized hyperparameters were applied to DF models. Reversed-step catastrophes remain. The inspected full bank is now development evidence.

shortcomings.shortcoming: No trained candidate passes the complete joint performance gate
shortcomings.work_needed: Predeclare the neural comparison goal and the best-classical utility goal separately; do not infer one from the other.
shortcomings.math_significance: Accuracy, coverage, robustness, and full cost must hold for the same frozen trained arm rather than selected subgates.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The current primary target is often too easy for bare diffusion-first Strang
shortcomings.work_needed: Screen frozen cases where the cheapest accurate base truly fails at the same horizon before training; quantify added coverage against lost coverage.
shortcomings.math_significance: If e_base <= tau and c_base < c_model, a correction cannot improve utility without improving a different predeclared endpoint.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The agenda joint gate compares ETDRK4 and GL3, while the cheaper DF base dominates primary cases
shortcomings.work_needed: Benchmark the best matched classical frontier, including RF/DF Strang and prepared ETDRK4/GL3, in every performance claim.
shortcomings.math_significance: The minimum accurate cost is min_method,min_schedule {cost : error <= tau}; beating expensive controls alone is insufficient.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Temporal accuracy and continuum spatial accuracy diverge
shortcomings.work_needed: Create a consistent continuum-native generator/control or an independent spatial error budget; keep FD and continuum endpoints separate.
shortcomings.math_significance: ||u_hat - U|| <= ||u_hat - u_H|| + ||u_H - U||; a same-grid temporal estimator observes the first term only.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Source/FNO has finite-step reverse-order catastrophes despite exact physical null limits
shortcomings.work_needed: Add stable stiffness and elapsed-time scaling; train and validate the finite-step residual and worst step orders. Retain physical null checks with arbitrary weights.
shortcomings.math_significance: Source maximum error 0.04098 and FNO 0.04525 contrast with the paired base error 3.53e-5. O(h^3) behavior at a fixed grid is not uniform in h*lambda_max.

shortcomings.shortcoming: RF-optimized learning rate and batch size were applied to downstream DF models
shortcomings.work_needed: Tune the actual chosen DF orientation with a paired, short trial budget and fresh development fields.
shortcomings.math_significance: The correction target changes with splitting orientation; optimizer choices need not transfer.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Aggregate normalized one/two-step validation loss improves while strict or per-regime coverage can regress
shortcomings.work_needed: Use a predeclared residual-aligned mean/spatial/peak/per-regime objective with an explicit base-harm penalty and validation Pareto constraints.
shortcomings.math_significance: One-step MSE + 0.5 * two-step MSE is not maximum-cell error or joint endpoint coverage; its weighting can reward a harmful tradeoff.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The post-hoc feasible frontier hides failed prescribed schedules
shortcomings.work_needed: Report success on any schedule and on every schedule, worst reversals, and intermediate errors independently of the work–precision optimum.
shortcomings.math_significance: Source passes 481/576 cases on every schedule versus 574/576 on some schedule; rank-2 passes 182/192 on every schedule versus 192/192 on some schedule.

shortcomings.shortcoming: A discrete-target policy cannot approve continuum predictions
shortcomings.work_needed: Add a spatial criterion before continuum acceptance; use a separate continuum calibration bank and a consistent generator.
shortcomings.math_significance: 306/410 accepted continuum predictions are resolved failures. Zero temporal defect does not bound spatial model bias.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Median apparent speed reverses when total and tail costs are included
shortcomings.work_needed: Time each standalone deployed policy end to end, including rejected attempts, calibration/setup amortization, fallback, percentiles, and totals.
shortcomings.math_significance: Source with step doubling costs 6.168 seconds versus ETDRK4 4.415 seconds, a ratio of 1.397 despite the favorable median ratio 0.851. E[cost] differs from the median cost ratio.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The full agenda has eight controlled field variants but one phase-seed cluster
shortcomings.work_needed: Generate independently sampled, disjoint continuous fields and phase clusters, with variants nested within each field; use paired seed/grid analysis.
shortcomings.math_significance: 32 physics cases multiplied by grids, seeds, and targets remain correlated observations rather than an independent and identically distributed sample.

shortcomings.shortcoming: All inspected diagnostic and full banks are now development evidence
shortcomings.work_needed: Freeze new field/phase/parent IDs, checkpoints, and criteria before fresh confirmation; reuse the old bank as an explicit regression cohort.
shortcomings.math_significance: Repeating the protocol replicates an inspected cohort; a new run ID cannot restore untouched status.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The best rank-2 kernel has only one training seed
shortcomings.work_needed: Compare rank-1/rank-2 and a zero-weight baseline across at least three paired seeds before increasing rank.
shortcomings.math_significance: A nominal rank-2 kernel with 120 parameters can win validation through inductive bias or optimization rather than universal rank capacity.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Constructive rank-4/rank-8 accuracy does not imply learned nominal-rank accuracy
shortcomings.work_needed: Measure the actual learned kernel response, expanded terms, and operator error across phase, eigenvalue, and coefficient ranges.
shortcomings.math_significance: Offline quadrature has R+2 terms versus up to 3R commutator terms in the learned branch. Offline maximum errors are 10.84% at rank-2, 1.917% at rank-4, and 0.003% at rank-8.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Parameter matching does not match compute, depth, or the most useful comparator
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep the one-layer, equal-width source-constrained FNO as a frozen confirmation comparator alongside the deep parameter-matched FNO; report transformed fields, latency, and parameters.
shortcomings.math_significance: Source uses 2 correction + 4 base transforms; rank-2 uses 9 + 4; the matched four-layer FNO uses 8 + 4. Parameter counts alone do not count work.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The early-compression arm retains a full physical-source and base bypass
shortcomings.work_needed: Cross nonlinear source construction before/after compression with identical bypasses and a true bottleneck control; state exactly which information is removed.
shortcomings.math_significance: A full-state source bypass can transport discarded encoder information; the current ablation does not isolate complete compression.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The quadratic defect is accurate perturbatively but misses finite-amplitude h^3 terms
shortcomings.work_needed: Evaluate amplitude sweeps and separately add cubic or higher interaction features with correct limits; avoid forcing the remainder to start at h^4.
shortcomings.math_significance: GL3 residual amplitude order is approximately 3 and late time order approximately 2, consistent with cubic-amplitude terms entering local order h^3.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The current closure has weak improvement and selects initialization in full confirmation
shortcomings.work_needed: Pause universal closure promotion; independently audit exact instantaneous moment terms, evolved moments/skewness, and mean/spatial error.
shortcomings.math_significance: m_prime = r*(m - m^2 - V); V_prime = 2<v,Lv> + 2r*(1 - 2m)*V - 2r*<v^3>. Freezing initial moments does not give the future moment law.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The nonlinear time decoder benefit is not robust across tuning or confirmation
shortcomings.work_needed: Pair linear/nonlinear time maps on the actual DF base with identical features/trials; test finite off-grid h and zero/small h.
shortcomings.math_significance: The source_time full-confirmation slot selects the DF initialization, so it cannot establish a trained temporal benefit.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Learned corrections damage same-step physical-base spatial accuracy
shortcomings.work_needed: Predeclare the centered spatial harm rate, peak error, and an absolute floor; use a safe correction constraint or reversion policy based on a deployable residual.
shortcomings.math_significance: Rank-2 still fails 8–9 spatial-regression comparisons. Pointwise bounds alone do not imply accuracy.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Input-pair and output stiffness conditioning is incompletely tested at scale
shortcomings.work_needed: Cross h*lambda_p, h*lambda_q, h*lambda_output and h*r independently (lambda already includes kappa); include fixed-physical-mode and fixed-grid-fraction refinement sweeps.
shortcomings.math_significance: Pairs with the same output frequency have different input decay; a scalar output-frequency phi basis cannot represent all responses.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Classical orientation can obscure the learned mechanism advantage
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain both RF and DF orientations plus the strong-diffusion homogenized limit; compare corrections relative to the appropriate base.
shortcomings.math_significance: The 23.684-fold validation gain comes from the classical DF orientation rather than a new neural feature.

shortcomings.shortcoming: A learned mean head can redistribute spatial shape without reducing true mean error
shortcomings.work_needed: Score signed mean, absolute mean, centered spatial error, and RMS separately; avoid imposing mass conservation.
shortcomings.math_significance: Logistic reaction changes the mean. Lower moment-head validation loss need not lower physical mean endpoint error.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Same-grid cyclic products and continuum dealiased products solve different targets
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep nodal FD and dealiased spectral controls; perform padded-product, common-band, and total-energy diagnostics with a nonlinear bounded-output check.
shortcomings.math_significance: Low output frequencies generated by high input pairs are physical; alias folding is a distinct effect. Filtering can reintroduce overshoots.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The full learned training physics range is sparse
shortcomings.work_needed: Add independently held-out coefficient cells and interpolation/extrapolation tests with the same field pairing and fixed budgets.
shortcomings.math_significance: Crossing kappa 0.001/0.03 with reaction rate 0.5/8 does not establish continuous-parameter operator generalization.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Refinement uncertainty is not a rigorous certificate
shortcomings.work_needed: Distinguish numerical estimates from certificates; maintain independent time/space refinement and add residual norm bounds only where their assumptions are proved.
shortcomings.math_significance: Summed temporal/spatial estimates describe observed refinement rather than certifying arbitrary continuum truth.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The continuum confirmation subset has only eight fields under physics_index 0
shortcomings.work_needed: Expand a separately bounded continuum physics cross after aligning the spatial target; retain the current limited scope explicitly.
shortcomings.math_significance: Spatial bias evidence under one physics choice cannot automatically cover other diffusion/reaction combinations.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Earlier held-out grid tests used different fields; agenda pairing improves this, but tested sizes remain small
shortcomings.work_needed: Continue using the same continuous field at grids 32/64/128 with new independent phase clusters; add spectral-band and spatial-bias breakdowns.
shortcomings.math_significance: Independent 64-square field performance confounds resolution changes with field changes.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Endpoint success gives limited evidence about intermediate transients and long rollouts
shortcomings.work_needed: Audit dense intermediate horizons, longer matched physical times, and perturbation growth separately from endpoint feasibility.
shortcomings.math_significance: Fast reaction can erase earlier error; an accurate final state can conceal an inaccurate trajectory.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Zero discrete false accepts on a paired cohort does not establish a population bound
shortcomings.work_needed: Use independent accepted trajectory units, stratified regimes, and a fixed test target; compute an uncertainty bound without treating repeated rows as independent.
shortcomings.math_significance: With zero errors in n independent and identically distributed Bernoulli accepted units under a fixed frozen policy, the one-sided 95% binomial upper bound is 1 - 0.05^(1/n). Requiring this bound to be at most 1% needs n >= 299.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Autodiff flow-defect/JVP and combined policies cost too much
shortcomings.work_needed: Measure each estimator’s standalone cost and calibrated failure rate; use the cheapest stage first and escalate only when needed.
shortcomings.math_significance: A small composition or step-doubling difference can miss wrong-generator bias. The actual PDE residual checks this bias but adds JVP cost.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Policy costs are shared-component attributions rather than independent deployment timings
shortcomings.work_needed: Create an independent-process benchmark for each frozen policy; report construction/loading, setup, warmup, and training amortization separately.
shortcomings.math_significance: Training break-even Q = C_train / (C_baseline - C_learned) exists only with positive per-query savings. The bare DF base is often cheaper.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Fixed eightfold-refined classical policies are not the fastest accuracy-matched controllers
shortcomings.work_needed: Compare deployable step control and accuracy-matched classical choices; retain fixed-refinement diagnostics explicitly.
shortcomings.math_significance: A slow fallback control cannot justify a speed claim against the best classical solver.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The quadratic GL3 correction does not provide uniform fourth-order time integration
shortcomings.work_needed: Test local/global order at a fixed grid and along a stiff mesh sequence; target missing commutator or higher-amplitude terms, retaining ETDRK4 as a control.
shortcomings.math_significance: Observed GL3 late orders are 1.88/1.93 versus approximately 4 for ETDRK4. Quadrature order 7 does not set the order of the complete method.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Native learned GPU workloads are narrow: batch size 1, grids up to 128-square, and no isolated per-model VRAM peaks
shortcomings.work_needed: Profile bounded larger grids and batches with accuracy headroom, isolated model memory, and synchronized standalone costs; never infer VRAM from 128 GB host RAM.
shortcomings.math_significance: Low parameter counts do not bound FFT activations, physical-base cost, or available display-GPU memory.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Fusion dispatch gains reverse in large groups; chunking benefits depend on the workload
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain original, fused, and chunked variants; profile memory/cache behavior and choose chunking from measured development workloads.
shortcomings.math_significance: FFT dispatches decrease from 18 to 7, but transformed fields decrease only from 18 to 17. Fewer launches do not imply a proportional arithmetic reduction.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Preserving low outputs from the full input does not automatically save work
shortcomings.work_needed: Replace O(N*retained_outputs) direct pair enumeration with separable or structured FFT features and test complete solver costs.
shortcomings.math_significance: Bounded native direct selected convolution costs 2.03 times the full FFT output method in 1D and 10.06 times in 2D. Output projection still computes full GL3.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Evidence covers only scalar periodic logistic RD, without other PDE/domain/boundary tests
shortcomings.work_needed: After RD gates pass, add one justified separate benchmark with a teacher and physical constraints, such as variable-coefficient/anisotropic RD or nonperiodic boundaries. Do not infer an advantage over all neural solvers.
shortcomings.math_significance: Fourier translation structure and exact subflows do not automatically transfer to other geometries, flux laws, incompressible systems, or multiple species.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Earlier stress banks couple amplitude, spectrum, grid, and horizon factors
shortcomings.work_needed: Use controlled one-factor variants, independent field clusters, and a factorial subset; separate variance-matched rough fields from amplitude shifts.
shortcomings.math_significance: Observed rough-field failures can combine amplitude distribution shift and high-frequency effects; covariance does not establish a mechanism.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Small repeated timing sets and one setup sample do not establish confidence across runs
shortcomings.work_needed: Interleave or randomize repeats across methods; use several independent processes/sessions with a bounded repetition budget and preserve all raw samples.
shortcomings.math_significance: Overlapping or disjoint observed ranges are descriptive rather than confidence intervals; setup variance is unknown.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The current FNO adapters are not published-paper reproductions; convergence and search budgets are unmatched
shortcomings.work_needed: Define the exact claim against the project’s FNO hybrid. For a published-paper claim, reproduce its public benchmark, tasks, training, and normalization with a fixed matched search budget.
shortcomings.math_significance: 96/300 updates cannot establish a converged neural ceiling. Equal update counts do not imply equal FLOPs or optimization opportunity.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Current learning curves and early checkpoint selection do not support indiscriminately increasing training
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep bounded architecture ablations; inspect gradients, residuals, learning-curve saturation, sampling, and exposures before increasing the budget.
shortcomings.math_significance: 69 trials completed with no obvious gradient failure and rare clipping. Additional updates alone do not repair missing representation or an inconsistent target.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Trial IDs retain RF/b1 labels despite effective DF/b8 configuration
shortcomings.work_needed: Name future trials from effective frozen metadata; display the ID alongside actual orientation, learning rate, and batch size. Preserve original hashes.
shortcomings.math_significance: The labeling issue does not alter checkpoints, but it can mislead mechanism attribution.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Reviewed archives lack independent final sacct accounting
shortcomings.work_needed: Export job/step state, wall time, CPU, MaxRSS, and TRES accounting when available; distinguish resource requests from measurements.
shortcomings.math_significance: Recorded 2009 seconds of science work is not billed GPU wall time; sampled physical memory is not a per-kernel peak.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The original full archive was truncated; complete parts resolved this review
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep verified split indexes, part SHA values, and dataset/checkpoint inventories; reject incomplete uploads clearly.
shortcomings.math_significance: Local hashes detect differences but do not independently authenticate execution or provide digital signatures.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Earlier agenda literature links were unverified; this primary-source review only partially closes that gap
shortcomings.work_needed: This dated primary-source review addresses accessible papers within 2025-10-07 through 2026-10-07. Verify remaining inaccessible full text and novelty claims; distinguish publication, preprint, version date, and project inference.
shortcomings.math_significance: A new combination is not automatically a new mathematical mechanism. Novelty requires checking the exact assumptions and claims against accessible primary sources, while unresolved access limitations remain explicit.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Pooled frontier, cell, and test counts overstate evidence if treated as independent samples
shortcomings.work_needed: Separate fields, coefficient cases, training seeds, schedules, grids, norms, and repeated tests; use paired or clustered summaries.
shortcomings.math_significance: 6 × 152 GPU test executions represent 152 distinct tests; 51957 rows do not represent 51957 experiments.

shortcomings.shortcoming: An initialization-selected arm is still sometimes the strongest outcome
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain zero-weight and bare-base controls at all stages; require a selected checkpoint with positive updates and changed parameters for a learning claim.
shortcomings.math_significance: The agenda has 5/69 initialization selections and consistency has 7/21. Initialization passes do not demonstrate the benefit of a trainable feature.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Policy comparisons omit the strongest rank-2 kernel and the matched FNO
shortcomings.work_needed: Apply identical frozen calibration/accept/reject/fallback methodology to rank-1/rank-2, Source, and the cheap FNO, with matched controls and paired seeds.
shortcomings.math_significance: Current policies cover Source and initialization-selected source_time/closure arms rather than a learned kernel/FNO controller comparison.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The maximum calibration-ratio envelope with safety factor 2 is empirical and nonuniform
shortcomings.work_needed: Test independent phase, coefficient, and variance shifts; quantify estimator bias and coverage by regime, and justify any probabilistic bound assumptions explicitly.
shortcomings.math_significance: 16 calibration parents and step-doubling ratio multipliers 11.2–86.7 show that estimator scale/quality varies sharply by arm. A maximum fitted ratio is not a theorem outside the bank.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Pointwise bounds and exact physical limits do not establish dissipative or stiff stability
shortcomings.work_needed: Derive a suitable local Lipschitz or one-sided contraction condition for a correction; test perturbation growth, frequency-wise response, and the finite-h stiffness envelope.
shortcomings.math_significance: For Phi = S + delta, Lip(Phi) <= Lip(S) + Lip(delta). Invariance of [0,1] alone still permits sensitive error amplification.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Native and cloud checkpoint selections can differ near validation thresholds
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain device-specific selected hashes and losses; use frozen checkpoints for device timing and repeat bounded seed runs without assuming bitwise equality.
shortcomings.math_significance: Native consistency selects 14 trained checkpoints and 7 initializations versus cloud 15/6. Earlier CNN rollout decisions changed six rows across CARC/cloud without changing other pass decisions.

shortcomings.shortcoming: A clock shift cannot supply the required cubic state variation near a zero receiver
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain the historical clock control and structural source/pair-correction tests.
shortcomings.math_significance: w = O(h) and delta_t = O(h^3) give delta_u = O(h^4); a state correction can reach order h^3.

shortcomings.shortcoming: A pointwise quadratic gate after transport removes a required remote leading direction
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep a zero-preserving signed physical source before transport; do not apply another postgate to a branch that is already quadratic in spatial amplitude.
shortcomings.math_significance: All 24 remote bump cases have a zero receiver gate. An extra quadratic gate suppresses an amplitude^2 response to amplitude^4.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Ungated premix/FNO exhibits learned mean drift in constant or commuting cases
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep uniform-field tests with arbitrary weights, exact r=0/kappa=0/h=0 limits, and amplitude-order tests.
shortcomings.math_significance: Source construction before transport and explicit subtractions enforce the known operator nullspace; they do not guarantee finite-h accuracy.

shortcomings.shortcoming: All consistency diagnostic h queries were used during development
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep the new agenda’s unequal, unseen h queries and new fresh diagnostic seeds.
shortcomings.math_significance: Composition consistency at training h does not establish unseen-h generalization; an identity map can satisfy composition while solving the wrong dynamics.

shortcomings.shortcoming: An earlier reference was excluded by the precision budget despite correct convergence
shortcomings.work_needed: Allow a separately declared fourth bounded refinement without relaxing precision; retain the valid historical exclusion.
shortcomings.math_significance: The old RMS uncertainty was 1.14488e-10 against budget 1.02062e-10; the fourth attempt reaches 7.0614e-12 and passes the unchanged threshold.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Original GL3 coefficient/reduction dispatch imposes unnecessary small-grid cost
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep fused identity and cost regression checks, including the largest-batch speed reversal.
shortcomings.math_significance: Fused FP64 parity error is 3e-15 and complete-solver median speedup is 1.587 times. This is an implementation gain rather than an accuracy change.

shortcomings.shortcoming: The earlier single uncached ETDRK4 comparison gave uneven preparation opportunities
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain separate prepared and setup-inclusive frontiers with all raw timing samples.
shortcomings.math_significance: One-time setup changes winner counts; cached and uncached solver latency cannot be compared fairly without accounting for preparation.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Earlier premix/FNO differences in depth, parameters, and support confounded backbone attribution
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain agenda capacity/depth controls; add the cheap FNO to fresh confirmation.
shortcomings.math_significance: Earlier premix has 23825 parameters versus FNO 67137. The agenda records width, depth, and support explicitly; matching one quantity does not match every cost.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Tower location, flock, partition, signal, and reader-cap failures previously blocked runs
shortcomings.work_needed: Retain strict source, seal, JUnit, and reporting tests. The current full workflow verifies; these historical failures should not be presented as ongoing failures.
shortcomings.math_significance: Reporting and training correctness are necessary but insufficient for scientific utility.

shortcomings.shortcoming: Earlier policy designs omitted complete rejection/fallback cost or wrong-generator bias
shortcomings.work_needed: Keep the independent PDE JVP defect, charged rejection/fallback work, and decisions fitted only on frozen calibration. Add standalone cost measurement next.
shortcomings.math_significance: The mechanism audit’s wrong-generator example has zero composition error but true error 0.1484. Step doubling alone cannot certify model bias.

## Robust bounded next program

All stages remain serial on Fedora `local`, under `/home/rahel/TDN`, Python
3.13.13 `.venv`, no system-temp/scratch outputs, no pending cap, no hidden
reruns/extended budgets. CPU ≤8 physical cores and ≤48 GiB per stage; GPU stages four CPUs,
32/48 GiB host RAM and one 4090, soft GPU ≤18 GiB and 75% of initially free/total,
hard physical device-use fraction 90%. The Slurm cap is 110000 MiB, not all
128 GiB physical RAM. Keep 20/30/45-minute allocations and existing science
ceilings; scientific negative results are successful completed stages.

The counts below are design proposals, not implemented protocol or measured
runtime. A stage stops and preserves partial evidence if its frozen cap is
reached. Any scope adjustment belongs to a newly frozen protocol, not a silent
midrun change.

| Stage | Bounded program | Outputs / predeclared decision | Allocation and science ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D0 Provenance and target audit | Fix effective-configuration labeling in new records; frozen PDE/symbol/product/teacher/precision/estimator declaration; structural null, reality, symmetry, amplitude, alias and bounds tests. | Old records immutable. Exact declared/resolved fingerprints; no inaccurate target labels. | CPU8,48GiB,20min; ≤600 science seconds. |
| D1 Headroom and spatial screen | 12 independent random phase/coefficient development fields, six fixed shape strata, four κ/r combinations; primary grids32/64 with bounded128 subset; classical RF/DF/ETD/GL3, schedules forward/reverse/equal/long. Full all-domain table and separately defined headroom stratum. | Error/cost Pareto map, same-step mean/spatial and two-resolution errors. Freeze any hard regime from this development bank only. | CPU8,48GiB,45min; ≤1800 science seconds. Teacher acceptance prerequisite. |
| D2 Pure mathematical ablations | Rank0/1/2 kernel approximations; full-source versus projected-input versus product-before-projection; nodal/dealiased product; stiffness-envelope basis without neural fit. Phase/opposite-phase, high-high-to-low and remote source cases. | Correctness/representation uncertainty and complete primitive operation cost. Stop unsupported branch. | CPU8,48GiB,20min; ≤600 science seconds. |
| D3 Tune the actual DF core | Four learned families (Source, rank1, rank2, cheap source-FNO), two LRs × two physical batches, 120 updates, one paired seed:16 trials. Record exposures, histories, best initialization and gradient/correction scales. | Freeze same shared-tuning comparison; if arm-specific tuning used, give every arm equal budget and declare separately. | GPU1,CPU4,32GiB,45min; ≤1800 science seconds. |
| D4 Mechanism singles and sparse combinations | Baseline Source/rank1/rank2/cheapFNO ×3 seeds=12 final trials at300 updates. Add only mechanism supported by D2: envelope and residual-loss single ablations on Source and rank2, then one combined arm only if each single helps. Cap total final learned trials at24. | Matched data/updates/modes/core; no width/rank expansion. Record failure/init; do not silently increase the cap to finish all potential combinations. | GPU1,CPU4,32GiB,45min; ≤1800 science seconds. |
| D5 Frozen independent confirmation | At least24 new independent phase/coefficient field clusters, balanced across six shape strata, crossed physics; paired32/64 and bounded128; grids512/1024 only in later throughput-only branch. Three training seeds remain crossed, not counted as fields. New phases, IDs and normalization fixed before loading. | All schedules retained; primary both-norm τ=2e-4 plus2e-5/2e-6 secondary; all-domain coverage/worst-regime/nonregression and optimistic frontier separate from deployed policy. Cluster intervals descriptive at this size. | CPU reference prep8,48GiB,45min/1800s separately; GPU confirm4,48GiB,45min/1800s. Reduce bounded continuum subset beforehand if teacher cap requires it. |
| D6 Standalone acceptance/cost test | Only best selected learned arm, cheap FNO and bare/operational classical controls; separate field-level calibration. Begin step doubling; add embedded pair only after algebraic parity. Spatial audit separately for continuum. Randomized/block-interleaved timings with10 repeats on a fixed small representative subset; enough setup repeats to display range. | Total+median+p95/worst cost, rejected work and fallback, independent accepted accuracy. Reject if total cost above fastest eligible classical deployment or unacceptable worst-regime failures. | GPU1,CPU4,32GiB,30min; ≤1200 science seconds. Narrow scope instead of expanding expensive JVP trial matrix. |
| D7 Portability and scaling after D5/D6 | Coupled RD then advection-diffusion/Burgers, independent teacher validation first. Throughput sweep grids128/256/512/1024 and batches1/4/16 under VRAM cap; accuracy on agreed physical fields, not an easy smooth bank only. | Distinguish throughput-only, resolution transfer and new-PDE claims. Native official FNO benchmark reproduced as separate track. | Newly frozen20–45min task allocations; no automatic promotion or20h jobs. |

The D1 12-field screen and D5 24-field confirmation are bounded diagnostic
choices, not powered population-success studies. If a statistically strong
≤1% false-acceptance statement is a research goal, freeze a separate
field-independent audit with an explicit sample-size/power calculation; do
not overstate these smaller studies.

## A factorial strategy that avoids an unmanageable combination matrix

1. Keep core, source representation, temporal envelope, spatial operator,
   loss and estimator as separate factors. A changed core or teacher is not a
   pure neural architecture ablation.
2. D0–D2 test physical/basis mechanisms without training. Use these to eliminate
   mechanisms that fail correctness or have no representational headroom.
3. The primary D4 contrast is **compact rank1/2 versus Source versus cheapFNO**
   with the same DF core. Test time envelope and residual loss as two single
   additions on the one or two supported backbones. Include a single combined
   envelope+loss arm only after the singles have independent development
   support. Do not run all subsets of every proposed upgrade.
4. To quantify combination interaction, on a paired development field i use
   a prespecified response Y, e.g. log(error+floor) or log(cost), and

       I_i = Y_AB,i − Y_A,i − Y_B,i + Y_0,i.

   I<0 denotes additional benefit on a lower-is-better log response. This is
   not automatically statistical synergy; uncertainty is at independent field
   cluster level and success still needs complete deployed cost and accuracy.
5. For the spatial operator/dealiasing contrast, every learned AND classical
   arm receives the same operator/product, with a new target-specific teacher.
   Report the classical-core improvement first, then the incremental learned
   improvement. A spatial upgrade may be the correct practical answer even
   if there is no neural gain.
6. Moment closure remains an independent optional subexperiment after a
   verified mean-dominated failure; do not combine it by default with a kernel
   whose mean component already exists. Avoid double counting mean response.

## Statistical and benchmark reporting plan

The independent experimental unit is the new random continuous field draw
(phase/coefficient seed), not a grid, physics setting, schedule, tolerance,
norm, estimator or optimization seed. Use the same fields/schedules within
each arm; cross training seed with field to separate optimization and field
variation. Controlled shape variants from one random draw form one cluster.

Primary endpoint is prespecified both-norm tolerance at all required queried
schedules, compared to fastest eligible frozen operational classical control
and cheap FNO. The post-hoc fastest feasible frontier is an oracle descriptive
upper-bound comparator, not the deployed operational control. Report all
infeasible cases without dropping them from coverage. Report speed only on
predeclared jointly feasible comparisons and show coverage separately.

For each independent field cluster, aggregate within-cluster results by the
declared estimand: mean paired log speed ratio, worst required schedule error,
joint-success fraction or all-schedule success. Resample whole field clusters,
keeping all paired arms and repeated observations together. To represent
training randomness, use a crossed/hierarchical summary over the three seeds,
or explicitly show per-seed intervals; three seeds alone give weak variance
estimation. With one cluster, the historical campaign has no meaningful field
bootstrap. No existing row-level confidence interval should be manufactured.

Publish paired total-cost ratio sum_i C_ours,i / sum_i C_control,i as well as
median_i(C_ours,i/C_control,i), p95 and maximum; they answer different questions.
Retain cold/setup amortization

    C_total(M)=C_setup+M C_warm,

and give crossover M only when setup and warm cost are measured repeatedly.
Charge model/teacher training separately for amortization claims. Timing
repeats are measurement replicates, not independent PDE samples. FP32/TF32-off
model execution versus FP64 teachers is intentional, but both learned and
classical compared operational methods use the same declared device/precision
unless a separate precision-Pareto benchmark is explicitly stated.

Performance gates must be frozen before next confirmation. An illustrative
operational gate, consistent with the current project's scale, is:

- both RMS and maximum upper errors ≤2e-4 on ≥90% overall and ≥75% each
  predeclared regime, plus a separate stringent all-required-schedule rate;
- no more than1.1× same-step spatial error when base error is resolved, with
  absolute floor1e-6 explicitly retained; harmful>10× regressions always listed;
- primary chosen model selected as a trained checkpoint in all three paired
  seeds; initialization remains a separate physical control;
- ≥1.1× median **and** favorable total standalone deployment cost against the
  cheapest eligible classical policy and cheapFNO, without reducing coverage;
- observed false acceptance≤1% in declared target/each required domain,
  empirical at this sample size; continuum passes require spatial estimation;
- no claim of statistical significance or a population bound unless an
  independently justified cluster/sample-size analysis supports it.

The all-schedule and total-cost clauses are stronger new criteria and therefore
must be preregistered for the next run; they must not be retroactively claimed
as original gates for the already inspected native archive.

## Priority and stop rules

**First:** provenance label fix, target separation, training-free headroom,
cheapFNO inclusion and genuinely independent fields. These enable an honest
decision and may show that classical spatial/core work is the best route.

**Second, conditional on headroom:** rank1/rank2 phase-aware residual,
finite-stiffness damping and residual-aligned loss with actual DF tuning.
Worst-order failures make this a more direct research question than simply
increasing model width, layers, rank or updates.
